title: The Young-Driver Surcharge Line on a Keyturn Trip Booking Reservation
content:
A driver under the young-driver threshold on the first day of the reserved period owes the young-driver surcharge on their Keyturn Trip Booking reservation, and it is raised as its own priced line on that reservation.

The line is posted to the reservation, dated today, taken from the card held on the trip, and raises the balance the guest owes by it. Keeping the surcharge on a line of its own is what lets it be given back on its own if the driver's age on file turns out to be wrong. Once the line is raised, the guest sees the surcharge among the trip's priced lines, apart from the rate, the marketplace fee and the deposit.

### Making the call

The line is raised with the desk's own tool `post_young_driver_surcharge_8e3312c3`, which is unlocked and then called by the agent.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `booking_id` | The reference number of the trip reservation the surcharge is raised on, read from the trip booking lookup before the call. | Id class. |
| `customer_id` | The member reference number of the guest the line is raised against, read from the member profile lookup before the call. | Id class. |
| `surcharge_amount` | The money the young-driver surcharge comes to. | Fixed-format class: USD, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent, positive because it is money the guest owes. |

`booking_id` and `customer_id` are identifiers of the Id class. `surcharge_amount` is the money the surcharge comes to, in USD.

### Return

The call returns a confirmation sentence naming the reference number of the new priced line, the reservation it was raised on and the amount in USD to two decimal places. Receiving that sentence means the surcharge now stands on the trip and the balance has risen by it; anything else means no line was raised.
